request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added review assignment for stewards, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does**
- **Stored data:** a new nullable column `claim.review_assigned`, added by migration `V113__claim_review_assigned.sql`.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{id}/assign-review`, which records the user on the claim (`ClaimService.assignReview`).
  - It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, a blank user, and any claim not in `REVIEW`. A refusal writes nothing.
  - A successful assignment writes `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … person= amount= date= user=<user>` to the audit file. When the assignment is made on another user's behalf (delegation), the app's audit service adds `for=<them>` itself.
  - The assigned user is now part of every claim the server returns.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row has a new "Review assigned to" column (`claim-review-assigned`), a user entry (`claim-review-user`) and an "Assign review" button (`claim-review-assign`). A refusal shows the row's existing `claim-error`.
  - The header shows "My reviews" (`my-reviews-count`): how many `REVIEW` claims are assigned to the signed-in user.

**Choices the request didn't settle**
- **Assignment stays after review.** When the claim moves back to `OPEN`, it still shows the assigned user, as the test expects. It no longer counts in "My reviews", because only `REVIEW` claims count.
- **No closed-period check.** Assigning a claim whose due-by falls in a closed period is allowed, because assignment changes no money. Other claim actions refuse in that case; if you want assignment to match them, it's a small change.
- **Matching is by exact sign-in name.** "My reviews" doesn't recognise a person's alias, which the "My due" figures appear to do.
- **The typed name isn't checked.** You can assign a claim to any name, even one with no role on the sheet.
